name: Jungle
summary: Jungle is chopped-break grammar, not composed groove: slices of a sampled funk break (Amen, Think, Apache, Hot Pants, Soul Pride, Cold Sweat, Funky Drummer) rearranged bar to bar into new sentences, with a dense ghost-note snare language over a sparse anchoring kick. Ragga jungle adds dancehall 3-3-2 kicks and rim/tom bounce; intelligent jungle washes the same DNA into ride/shaker atmosphere over a deep sub kick.

sounds.kick: The break's own kick, reinforced with a sub-heavy 808/909 layer for low-end the sampled hit alone rarely has; sparse placement (beat 1 plus one syncopated hit) rather than a 4/4 pulse.
sounds.snare: The break's snare (Amen/Think/Soul Pride) chopped into hits and re-triggered with dense low-velocity ghost chatter around the 2-and-4 backbeat, often doubled with an 808/909 snare or clap for extra crack; timestretched pitch gives the classic robotic snare-roll shimmer.
sounds.hats: Ride/hat/tambourine slices lifted straight from the source break (Think's tambourine, Apache's ride) for constant top-end motion, sometimes topped up with a programmed 909/707 closed hat.
sounds.percussion: Conga/bongo lattices chopped from Apache, funk ghost accents from Hot Pants, and reverb/delay-treated rim/tom hits for ragga bounce - all sample-sourced rather than synthesized.
sounds.cymbals: A single reversed or forward crash at section changes; the ride is a groove element carried over from the source break, not a wash.

machines: 10 Most Iconic Amen Patterns pack — the primary Amen source material for chopping (owned)
junglebreaks.co.uk collection — classic pre-chopped jungle break library (owned)
Neekeetone Jungle Breaks — curated break pack for modern revival chops (owned)
Assorted funk/soul break library — Think, Apache, Hot Pants, Soul Pride, Cold Sweat, Funky Drummer, Tighten Up source loops (owned)
Akai S900 / S950 — the samplers that turned breaks into a chopped vocabulary; the S950's timestretching is the source of jungle's pitched-up snare-roll crunch (owned)
Akai S1000 / S5000 — higher-fidelity timestretch and multi-sampling for 2000s-onward revival chops (owned)
Akai MPC60 / MPC2000 / MPC3000 / MPC4000 — break slicing, pad-mapping and sequencing across every jungle era (owned)
E-mu SP-1200 / SP-12 / Drumulator — 12-bit resampling grit on hats, snares and kicks pulled from the break (owned)
Roland TR-808 / TR-909 — sub-reinforcement kick layer and synth snare/clap doubling under the sampled break (owned)
Roland TR-727 / TR-505 / TR-707 — programmed conga, rimshot and hat layers filling gaps around the chop (owned)
Casio SK-1 — lo-fi sampling of vocal stabs, sirens and found sound for MC/ragga intros (owned)
Ensoniq ASR-X / Akai S900 successors — modern break-chopping workflow for revival jungle (owned)
